item.text: The schema distinguishes clinical changes from corrections: holds persist until resumed or stopped, reviews don’t refresh list entries, and lab corrections can withdraw a value. I’m handling item history before replaying the lists, with Chicago-local dates for the as-of cutoff.

I’m preserving the source’s coding limits: medication RxNorm codes describe products, while allergy RxNorm codes identify ingredients. I’ll retain stated date precision and CKD stages, convert platelet and white-cell counts from cells/µL, and exclude billing diagnoses and narrative-only measurements.

The mapper passes the strict type check and sample harness. I’m now testing cases the samples don’t cover: correction chains, retractions, late-recorded events, medication restarts, persistent holds, and lab copies that must resolve to one result without losing a separate redraw.

Implemented `out/transform.ts`. The strict harness and all 25 tests pass.

Judgment calls: holds persist until explicitly changed; reviews don’t refresh state. Referral diagnoses fill missing problem history without overriding list events. Billing diagnoses are excluded. Product RxNorm codes aren’t treated as ingredient codes, and CKD stages aren’t inferred from labs.
